lines.text: And some businesses just don't have the finance needed to grow.
lines.say: And some businesses just don't have the finance needed to grow.

lines.text: Sadly, many businesses fail. What are the main causes?
lines.say: Sadly, many businesses fail. What are the main causes?

lines.text: A lack of management skills: owners without experience may make poor decisions about pricing, stock, or staff.
lines.say: A lack of management skills: owners without experience may make poor decisions about pricing, stock, or staff.

lines.text: Changes in the business environment: a new competitor arrives, consumer tastes change, new technology appears, or the economy falls into recession.
lines.say: Changes in the business environment: a new competitor arrives, consumer tastes change, new technology appears, or the economy falls into recession.

lines.text: And liquidity problems, which means running out of cash. A business can be selling well, and even making a profit, but if it can't pay its suppliers and workers on time, it may be forced to close.
lines.say: And liquidity problems, which means running out of cash. A business can be selling well, and even making a profit, but if it can't pay its suppliers and workers on time, it may be forced to close.

lines.text: Other causes include poor planning, and expanding too quickly.
lines.say: Other causes include poor planning, and expanding too quickly.

lines.text: New businesses are at an especially high risk of failure. Why?
lines.say: New businesses are at an especially high risk of failure. Why?

lines.text: Their owners often have little experience of running a business.
lines.say: Their owners often have little experience of running a business.

lines.text: They have few customers, and nobody knows their brand yet.
lines.say: They have few customers, and nobody knows their brand yet.

lines.text: They have limited finance, and no cash reserves to fall back on.
lines.say: They have limited finance, and no cash reserves to fall back on.

lines.text: And they face tough competition from established firms, which already have loyal customers, and lower costs.

lines.text: Chapter four. Types of business organisation. When someone starts a business, one of the first decisions is which legal form it should take.
lines.say: Chapter four. Types of business organisation. When someone starts a business, one of the first decisions is which legal form it should take.

lines.text: To understand the different types, you need one key idea first: liability.
lines.say: To understand the different types, you need one key idea first: liability.

lines.text: Unlimited liability means the owners are personally responsible for all the debts of the business. If the business can't pay, the owners may have to sell their own possessions, like their car, or even their house.
lines.say: Unlimited liability means the owners are personally responsible for all the debts of the business. If the business can't pay, the owners may have to sell their own possessions, like their car, or even their house.

lines.text: Limited liability means the owners can only lose the money they invested in the business. Their personal possessions are safe.
lines.say: Limited liability means the owners can only lose the money they invested in the business. Their personal possessions are safe.

lines.text: Businesses with limited liability are called limited companies, or incorporated businesses. They have a separate legal identity from their owners, so the company itself can own property, sign contracts, sue, and be sued.
lines.say: Businesses with limited liability are called limited companies, or incorporated businesses. They have a separate legal identity from their owners, so the company itself can own property, sign contracts, sue, and be sued.

lines.text: Let's start with the simplest. A sole trader is a business owned and controlled by just one person, although it can still employ other workers. Many small shops, hairdressers, and plumbers are sole traders.
lines.say: Let's start with the simplest. A sole trader is a business owned and controlled by just one person, although it can still employ other workers. Many small shops, hairdressers, and plumbers are sole traders.

lines.text: Sole traders are easy and cheap to set up, with very few legal formalities. The owner keeps all of the profit, and has complete control, so decisions can be made quickly.
lines.say: Sole traders are easy and cheap to set up, with very few legal formalities. The owner keeps all of the profit, and has complete control, so decisions can be made quickly.

lines.text: But the owner has unlimited liability. Raising capital is difficult, the hours are long, and there's nobody to share the work with. And the business may end if the owner becomes ill or dies, which is called a lack of continuity.
lines.say: But the owner has unlimited liability. Raising capital is difficult, the hours are long, and there's nobody to share the work with. And the business may end if the owner becomes ill or dies, which is called a lack of continuity.

lines.text: A partnership is a business owned by two or more people, usually up to twenty. Partners often sign a partnership agreement, which sets out how much capital each partner puts in, how profits are shared, and what happens if a partner leaves.
lines.say: A partnership is a business owned by two or more people, usually up to twenty. Partners often sign a partnership agreement, which sets out how much capital each partner puts in, how profits are shared, and what happens if a partner leaves.

lines.text: Compared with a sole trader, there's more capital available, and partners can share the workload, their skills, and any losses.
lines.say: Compared with a sole trader, there's more capital available, and partners can share the workload, their skills, and any losses.

lines.text: But in most partnerships, the partners still have unlimited liability. Partners can disagree, profits have to be shared, and if a partner leaves or dies, the partnership may have to end.
lines.say: But in most partnerships, the partners still have unlimited liability. Partners can disagree, profits have to be shared, and if a partner leaves or dies, the partnership may have to end.

lines.text: The next two types are limited companies, which are owned by shareholders.
lines.say: The next two types are limited companies, which are owned by shareholders.

lines.text: A share is a small part of the ownership of a company. If you own shares, you're a shareholder, and you may receive part of the profits, called a dividend.
lines.say: A share is a small part of the ownership of a company. If you own shares, you're a shareholder, and you may receive part of the profits, called a dividend.

lines.text: Shareholders elect a board of directors, to run the company on their behalf.
lines.say: Shareholders elect a board of directors, to run the company on their behalf.

lines.text: A private limited company, shown by the letters Ltd after its name, sells shares privately, to people the owners choose, such as family and friends. Its shares cannot be sold to the general public.
lines.say: A private limited company, shown by the letters L, T, D, after its name, sells shares privately, to people the owners choose, such as family and friends. Its shares cannot be sold to the general public.

lines.text: Shareholders have limited liability. The company has a separate legal identity, and continuity, so it carries on even if a shareholder dies. It can raise more capital than a partnership, and the original owners keep control.
lines.say: Shareholders have limited liability. The company has a separate legal identity, and continuity, so it carries on even if a shareholder dies. It can raise more capital than a partnership, and the original owners keep control.

lines.text: But there are more legal formalities to set it up. The accounts must be published, so there's less privacy. And the amount of capital is still limited, because shares can't be sold to the public.
lines.say: But there are more legal formalities to set it up. The accounts must be published, so there's less privacy. And the amount of capital is still limited, because shares can't be sold to the public.

lines.text: A public limited company, or plc, can sell its shares to the general public, usually through a stock exchange. Most of the world's biggest companies are public limited companies.
lines.say: A public limited company, or P L C, can sell its shares to the general public, usually through a stock exchange. Most of the world's biggest companies are public limited companies.

lines.text: This means it can raise huge amounts of capital. Shareholders have limited liability, the company has continuity, and its size makes it easier to borrow money.
lines.say: This means it can raise huge amounts of capital. Shareholders have limited liability, the company has continuity, and its size makes it easier to borrow money.

lines.text: But setting up and running a plc is expensive, with strict legal rules. Its accounts are public, so competitors can see them. Because anyone can buy its shares, it can face a takeover. And there's a separation of ownership and control: shareholders own the company, but directors control it, and they may want different things.
lines.say: But setting up and running a P L C is expensive, with strict legal rules. Its accounts are public, so competitors can see them. Because anyone can buy its shares, it can face a takeover. And there's a separation of ownership and control: shareholders own the company, but directors control it, and they may want different things.

lines.text: A franchise is when a business, called the franchisor, sells the right to use its brand name, products, and way of doing business, to another business, called the franchisee.
lines.say: A franchise is when a business, called the franchisor, sells the right to use its brand name, products, and way of doing business, to another business, called the franchisee.

lines.text: The franchisee pays an initial fee, and then a royalty, which is a percentage of its sales, usually every year.
lines.say: The franchisee pays an initial fee, and then a royalty, which is a percentage of its sales, usually every year.

lines.text: In return, the franchisor provides the brand, training, supplies, and national advertising. Many fast-food restaurants, hotels, and gyms work this way.
lines.say: In return, the franchisor provides the brand, training, supplies, and national advertising. Many fast-food restaurants, hotels, and gyms work this way.

lines.text: For the franchisor, it's a fast way to expand without needing much capital, and franchisees work hard, because they've invested their own money.
lines.say: For the franchisor, it's a fast way to expand without needing much capital, and franchisees work hard, because they've invested their own money.

lines.text: The risk is that one badly run franchise could damage the reputation of the whole brand, and profits are shared with the franchisees.
lines.say: The risk is that one badly run franchise could damage the reputation of the whole brand, and profits are shared with the franchisees.

lines.text: For the franchisee, the risk of failure is lower, because the brand is already well known, and they receive training and support.
lines.say: For the franchisee, the risk of failure is lower, because the brand is already well known, and they receive training and support.

lines.text: But they pay fees and royalties, must follow strict rules, and have little freedom to make their own decisions.
lines.say: But they pay fees and royalties, must follow strict rules, and have little freedom to make their own decisions.

lines.text: A joint venture is when two or more businesses agree to work together on a particular project, creating a separate business unit, and sharing its costs, risks, and profits.
lines.say: A joint venture is when two or more businesses agree to work together on a particular project, creating a separate business unit, and sharing its costs, risks, and profits.

lines.text: For example, a foreign car maker might team up with a local company to enter a new country, using the local company's knowledge of that market.
lines.say: For example, a foreign car maker might team up with a local company to enter a new country, using the local company's knowledge of that market.

lines.text: Joint ventures share costs and risks, and combine the expertise of both partners.
lines.say: Joint ventures share costs and risks, and combine the expertise of both partners.

lines.text: But the profits must be shared, and the partners may disagree, especially if they have different ways of working.
lines.say: But the profits must be shared, and the partners may disagree, especially if they have different ways of working.

lines.text: Finally, back to the public sector. A public corporation is a business owned and controlled by the government, on behalf of the public. Examples can include national railways, postal services, state broadcasters, and water companies.
lines.say: Finally, back to the public sector. A public corporation is a business owned and controlled by the government, on behalf of the public. Examples can include national railways, postal services, state broadcasters, and water companies.

lines.text: Its main aim is usually to provide an essential service at an affordable price, and to protect jobs, rather than simply to make a profit.
lines.say: Its main aim is usually to provide an essential service at an affordable price, and to protect jobs, rather than simply to make a profit.

lines.text: However, because the government will often cover its losses, there may be less incentive to be efficient, and it can become a burden on taxpayers.
lines.say: However, because the government will often cover its losses, there may be less incentive to be efficient, and it can become a burden on taxpayers.

lines.text: Let's put the main types side by side.
lines.say: Let's put the main types side by side.

lines.text: Sole traders have one owner, unlimited liability, and limited capital.
lines.say: Sole traders have one owner, unlimited liability, and limited capital.

lines.text: Partnerships have more owners and more capital, but still unlimited liability.
lines.say: Partnerships have more owners and more capital, but still unlimited liability.

lines.text: Private limited companies give limited liability and continuity, with shares sold privately.
lines.say: Private limited companies give limited liability and continuity, with shares sold privately.

lines.text: And public limited companies can raise the most capital of all, by selling shares to the public.
lines.say: And public limited companies can raise the most capital of all, by selling shares to the public.

lines.text: In an exam, the best type of organisation depends on how much capital is needed, how much risk the owners will accept, and how much control they want to keep.
lines.say: In an exam, the best type of organisation depends on how much capital is needed, how much risk the owners will accept, and how much control they want to keep.

lines.text: Chapter five. Business objectives and stakeholders. Every business needs to know where it's going, and who it answers to.
lines.say: Chapter five. Business objectives and stakeholders. Every business needs to know where it's going, and who it answers to.

lines.text: Business objectives are the aims, or targets, that a business works towards.
lines.say: Business objectives are the aims, or targets, that a business works towards.

lines.text: They give the business a clear direction and focus.
lines.say: They give the business a clear direction and focus.

lines.text: They motivate employees, who know exactly what they're working towards.
lines.say: They motivate employees, who know exactly what they're working towards.

lines.text: They make it possible to measure success, by comparing actual performance with the target.
lines.say: They make it possible to measure success, by comparing actual performance with the target.

lines.text: And they guide decision-making, helping managers choose between different options.
lines.say: And they guide decision-making, helping managers choose between different options.

lines.text: The best objectives are SMART: specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time-bound.
lines.say: The best objectives are SMART: specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time-bound.

lines.text: For example: increase sales by 10% within the next 12 months. It's specific, measurable, realistic, and it has a deadline.
lines.say: For example: increase sales by ten percent within the next twelve months. It's specific, measurable, realistic, and it has a deadline.

lines.text: So what objectives do businesses set? Here are the four big ones.
lines.say: So what objectives do businesses set? Here are the four big ones.

lines.text: Survival: simply staying in business. This is the main objective for new businesses, and for any business during a recession, or when a powerful new competitor arrives.
lines.say: Survival: simply staying in business. This is the main objective for new businesses, and for any business during a recession, or when a powerful new competitor arrives.

lines.text: Profit: the reward for the owners, and a source of money to reinvest in the business.
lines.say: Profit: the reward for the owners, and a source of money to reinvest in the business.

lines.text: Growth: increasing the size of the business, for example in sales, or the number of outlets, which can bring economies of scale, and more security.
lines.say: Growth: increasing the size of the business, for example in sales, or the number of outlets, which can bring economies of scale, and more security.

lines.text: And market share: the percentage of total market sales made by one business. A high market share gives a business status, and more power over suppliers and retailers.
lines.say: And market share: the percentage of total market sales made by one business. A high market share gives a business status, and more power over suppliers and retailers.

lines.text: Objectives also change over time. A brand new business may focus on survival, but once it's established, it may aim for growth, profit, or market share.
lines.say: Objectives also change over time. A brand new business may focus on survival, but once it's established, it may aim for growth, profit, or market share.

lines.text: Market share is calculated as the firm's sales, divided by the total sales in the market, multiplied by 100.
lines.say: Market share is calculated as the firm's sales, divided by the total sales in the market, multiplied by one hundred.

lines.text: So if a business sells $2 million worth of trainers, in a market worth $10 million,
lines.say: So if a business sells two million dollars' worth of trainers, in a market worth ten million dollars,

lines.text: its market share is 20%.
lines.say: its market share is twenty percent.

lines.text: Some businesses have very different priorities. A social enterprise is a business whose main objectives are social, or environmental. It still tries to make a profit, but it uses that profit to help people, or the planet.
lines.say: Some businesses have very different priorities. A social enterprise is a business whose main objectives are social, or environmental. It still tries to make a profit, but it uses that profit to help people, or the planet.

lines.text: For example, a café that trains and employs homeless people, or a company that sells bottled water, and uses its profits to build wells in communities without clean water.
lines.say: For example, a café that trains and employs homeless people, or a company that sells bottled water, and uses its profits to build wells in communities without clean water.

lines.text: Social enterprises often aim for a triple bottom line.
lines.say: Social enterprises often aim for a triple bottom line.

lines.text: Economic: making a profit.
lines.say: Economic: making a profit.

lines.text: Social: helping people and communities.
lines.say: Social: helping people and communities.

lines.text: And environmental: protecting the planet. These are often called profit, people, and planet.
lines.say: And environmental: protecting the planet. These are often called profit, people, and planet.

lines.text: Every business affects lots of different people. A stakeholder is any person or group with an interest in the activities and performance of a business.
lines.say: Every business affects lots of different people. A stakeholder is any person or group with an interest in the activities and performance of a business.

lines.text: Internal stakeholders are inside the business: the owners or shareholders, the managers, and the employees.
lines.say: Internal stakeholders are inside the business: the owners or shareholders, the managers, and the employees.

lines.text: External stakeholders are outside the business: customers, suppliers, lenders such as banks, the government, and the local community.
lines.say: External stakeholders are outside the business: customers, suppliers, lenders such as banks, the government, and the local community.

lines.text: Each stakeholder group wants something different from the business.
lines.say: Each stakeholder group wants something different from the business.

lines.text: Owners and shareholders want high profits, dividends, and a rising share price.
lines.say: Owners and shareholders want high profits, dividends, and a rising share price.

lines.text: Managers want good salaries, power and status, and job security.
lines.say: Managers want good salaries, power and status, and job security.

lines.text: Employees want fair pay, good working conditions, job security, and opportunities for training.
lines.say: Employees want fair pay, good working conditions, job security, and opportunities for training.

lines.text: Customers want good-quality products, at reasonable prices, with good service.
lines.say: Customers want good-quality products, at reasonable prices, with good service.

lines.text: Suppliers want regular orders, and to be paid on time.
lines.say: Suppliers want regular orders, and to be paid on time.

lines.text: Banks and other lenders want their loans repaid on time, with interest.
lines.say: Banks and other lenders want their loans repaid on time, with interest.

lines.text: The government wants the business to create jobs, pay its taxes, and obey the law.
lines.say: The government wants the business to create jobs, pay its taxes, and obey the law.

lines.text: And the local community wants jobs for local people, with little pollution, and a safe environment.
lines.say: And the local community wants jobs for local people, with little pollution, and a safe environment.

lines.text: Here's the problem: these objectives often conflict.
lines.say: Here's the problem: these objectives often conflict.

lines.text: Shareholders want higher profits. One way to achieve that is to cut costs, perhaps by replacing workers with machines. That's good for shareholders, but bad for employees, who want job security.
lines.say: Shareholders want higher profits. One way to achieve that is to cut costs, perhaps by replacing workers with machines. That's good for shareholders, but bad for employees, who want job security.

lines.text: Or imagine a business that wants to build a new factory. The government is pleased about the new jobs, but local residents may be unhappy about the extra noise, traffic, and pollution.
lines.say: Or imagine a business that wants to build a new factory. The government is pleased about the new jobs, but local residents may be unhappy about the extra noise, traffic, and pollution.

lines.text: And customers want low prices, while owners want high profits.
lines.say: And customers want low prices, while owners want high profits.

lines.text: A business can't keep everyone happy all the time. It has to prioritise, and find a compromise.
lines.say: A business can't keep everyone happy all the time. It has to prioritise, and find a compromise.

lines.text: Finally, objectives depend on which sector an organisation is in.
lines.say: Finally, objectives depend on which sector an organisation is in.

lines.text: Private sector businesses usually aim for survival, profit, growth, and market share.
lines.say: Private sector businesses usually aim for survival, profit, growth, and market share.

lines.text: Public sector organisations usually aim to provide a good service to the public, keep prices affordable so that everyone can use the service, protect jobs, and stay within the budget set by the government.
lines.say: Public sector organisations usually aim to provide a good service to the public, keep prices affordable so that everyone can use the service, protect jobs, and stay within the budget set by the government.

lines.text: Let's bring it all together.
lines.say: Let's bring it all together.

lines.text: Businesses exist to satisfy needs and wants, by combining scarce resources, and they succeed by adding value.
lines.say: Businesses exist to satisfy needs and wants, by combining scarce resources, and they succeed by adding value.

lines.text: They are classified into the primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, and into the private and public sectors.
lines.say: They are classified into the primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, and into the private and public sectors.

lines.text: Entrepreneurs start them. They grow internally or externally, and they can fail if they run out of cash, or fail to adapt.
lines.say: Entrepreneurs start them. They grow internally or externally, and they can fail if they run out of cash, or fail to adapt.

lines.text: They take different legal forms, from sole traders to public limited companies, each with its own balance of risk, capital, and control.
lines.say: They take different legal forms, from sole traders to public limited companies, each with its own balance of risk, capital, and control.

lines.text: And they set objectives, while balancing the conflicting interests of their stakeholders.
lines.say: And they set objectives, while balancing the conflicting interests of their stakeholders.

lines.text: Before you go, here are three exam tips.
lines.say: Before you go, here are three exam tips.

lines.text: One: learn your definitions word for word. Terms like added value, opportunity cost, and limited liability are easy marks.
lines.say: One: learn your definitions word for word. Terms like added value, opportunity cost, and limited liability are easy marks.

lines.text: Two: always apply your answer to the business in the question. Use its name, its products, and its situation, not just general points.
lines.say: Two: always apply your answer to the business in the question. Use its name, its products, and its situation, not just general points.

lines.text: And three: when a question asks you to evaluate, or discuss, look at both sides, and finish with a clear, justified conclusion.
